assumptions.statement: V_l is finite with no uniform upper bound, and X_l is the finite product of standard-Borel coordinate spaces.
rho_l is a probability law, m_l=exp(-H_l)rho_l has finite strictly positive mass, and pi_l is its normalization.
K_l is normalized, positive, measurable, and parameter independent; rho_l K_l and m_l K_l define the next measure pair.
A fixed jointly measurable reverse-kernel version Pi_l(dx|z) disintegrates pi_l(dx)K_l(x,dz).
The nonlinear action chart is an open L-infinity ball; every required exponential and derivative is uniformly bounded there.

At every admitted scale the interaction tier has finite standard-Borel product structure, a declared product probability nu_l equivalent to pi_l, and every nonempty subset interaction in hierarchical zero-mean gauge. Admission of a scale arrow separately requires pi_l K_l to be equivalent to a declared target product reference. Interaction-degree covariance uses a componentwise/permutation Borel realization or another explicitly proved grading intertwiner.

Each retained interaction space is closed and has a declared bounded idempotent projection with a declared operator norm and quotient residual norm; a gauge-covariant retained theory additionally requires the projection to intertwine the declared gauge realization.
One principal G-bundle induces belief and model statistical bundles; actions, references, kernels, sections, connections, and scale morphisms carry the stated equivariance data.
Statistical paths are differentiable in quadratic mean with centered finite-L2 scores, and parameter-independent pushforwards stay in the selected coarse family.
For the explicit spectral realization, X_i are iid N(0,1), b>=2, Z=b^(-1/2)sum_i X_i, and Hermites use the normalized probabilists' convention.
Ordinary spectra, fixed points, and beta differences use declared bounded scale isomorphisms J_l to one normed reference object.
Generalized mode sections have fixed norm, sign or phase, and per-volume normalization; only tempered scale-gauge changes are admitted as equivalences.

At each scale where a configuration claim is considered, Task 10 names a candidate configuration object Q_l, the declared gauge and base data used to type it, and a candidate coarse symbol mathsf R_l. This data-only label asserts no nonemptiness, manifold or smooth structure, metric, objective, vector field, projectability, or construction of the manuscript's own configuration map; each such property is an explicit hypothesis in the relevant claim quantifier or source theorem.

Kernel RN, kernel-KL, disintegration, and randomization claims use standard-Borel targets; every density tier has one fixed family-level sigma-finite reference and finite jointly measurable density versions, fixed sigma-finite integration is localized to finite-measure pieces, fixed-observation formulas use declared measurable RCP versions, and signed integrals obey the stated no-infinity-cancellation condition.

At each selected observation the evidence slice M_o has mass z in (0,infinity) and posterior Pi_o=M_o/z; L_ext=log z-KL(Q||Pi_o) is primary for every probability Q, while the classical expected-log split additionally requires Q<<Pi_o and separate H4 log-integrability.

An operational environment node is a standard-Borel state law plus a normalized measurable message kernel; this types an observation kernel as an interaction without asserting biological autonomy or deleting the conditioning sigma-algebra.

Variational attention is represented by finite normalized categorical source labels with positive priors and finite measurable source energies. On the selected complete-record slice the augmented likelihood is exactly a finite measurable label-free latent factor times the displayed per-label observation factors, no other record or generative factor reads any source label, normalization over the full record space is declared model data, and the constant-row softmax additionally assumes the separate recognition factorization.
Every external theorem or attribution uses a checked primary source or authoritative monograph with an exact statement and hypothesis mapping.

Chapter 12 uses external philosophical positions only as explicitly cited interpretive vocabulary; manuscript-specific idle-wheel, ontological-fit, and operational-holonomy claims remain separately status-tagged and require their own bridge or settlement evidence.
Numerical stability claims use deterministic controls through condition number 10^14, high-precision comparisons, scale-aware error bounds, and machine-readable JUnit output.
Verification binds the complete declared input policy, separates update from nonmutating verify mode, and records source revision, UTC timestamp, and semantic payload digest.

The Task 10 modeling scope declares no bridge from its mathematical duration to a physical clock reading and introduces no physical time, Lorentzian signature, causal structure, or canonical connection. The symbol ell is a declared discrete scale index and r is a chosen parameter of a curve. Tau is defined only after a configuration metric, a path, an origin, and an orientation have been selected.

The scale channel carries one family-level sigma-finite dominating measure with a fixed jointly measurable density version; K_l(x,X_{l+1})=1 for every x rather than almost every x; family closure N_*(B_l) subset B_{l+1} holds with the induced law-fiber map q smooth between the declared parametrized-measure models; the coarse-scale instance of the regular-model hypothesis holds, so the coarse Fisher form is invariant under its represented action; and a jointly measurable parameter-smooth version of the vertical differential is selected.

On the compatible/pullback-positivity branch, the declared scale-connection defect form A_frak = P_l^* omegabar - d kappa . omega takes values in the isotropy subalgebra of the coarse section value under the represented action.

For the finite branch, the primitive data are a base measure and strictly positive weight, a fixed positive-definite covariance, and finitely many basis fields that are independent in the stated weighted-L2 pairing. Where affine gauge closure is invoked, the basis span contains the relevant constant fields, the coefficient action xi -> xi + L_l g is separately declared, and a cross-scale coefficient map E is required to satisfy E L_l=L_{l+1}. For the L2 branch, the primitive data are two-sided bounds on the weight and fiber Fisher form together with a C1-on-L2 objective. These are applicability hypotheses only; regularity, gauge closure, and nonemptiness are conclusions of the exhibited finite-tier derivation or require separate verification on another tier.

At every scale arrow at which an integrated configuration metric or a duration is compared across scales, the two declaration conditions hold: (X1) f_# mu = mubar, and (X2) wbar_x . f <= w_x for both channels. Neither follows from any fiberwise contraction theorem.

Where an averaging or variational coarse configuration map is used, the declared affine chart of the coarse fiber makes (betabar,v) -> gbar^F_betabar(v,v) jointly convex; the constant-metric special case is used for the exact three-term identity. This fails in the covariance sector of the Gaussian moment chart and holds in the fixed-covariance location sector and in the law chart.

claims.statement: For every finite standard-Borel agent network of arbitrary finite cardinality, every finite interaction hypergraph on it, and every normalized parameter-independent blocking channel satisfying the declared domination, product-factor, gauge-equivariance, smoothness, and integrability hypotheses, construct a typed scale-indexed measure-pair, action, full-interaction, score-tangent, bundle, configuration, and history theory whose exact coarse maps, derivatives, contractions, defects, generalized modes, cocycles, beta data, fixed objects, pullback compatibilities, extended ELBO identities, and exact-versus-projected boundaries satisfy the obligations atomized in the bound claim ledger.

claims.statement: Centering is forced on any quadratic-mean tangent, and every centered h in L2 is realized two-sided by the normalized squared-linear path p_t=(1+th/2)^2/(1+t^2||h||^2/4). The iid product score is I_b h=sum_i h(X_i) with exact norm ||I_b h||^2=b||h||^2, the pushed score under a normalized parameter-independent kernel is L_b h=E[I_b h|Z], and the exact information budget is b||h||^2-||L_b h||^2=E Var(I_b h|Z)>=0 with equality exactly when I_b h is jointly almost surely coarse measurable. The bounded action quotient embeds isometrically in the Fisher norm onto the bounded centered subspace of L2_0, which is dense and generally proper, so its Fisher completion is L2_0; the L-infinity nonlinear action chart and the L2 quadratic-mean tangent remain distinct domains.

claims.statement: For the unit-variance block statistic Z=b^(-1/2)sum_i X_i at the standard Gaussian law, L_b e_k=b^(1-k/2)e_k for every k>=1 in the normalized probabilists' Hermite basis, that basis is complete in L2_0, and L_b is a positive self-adjoint diagonal Hilbert-Schmidt operator with sum of squared eigenvalues b^2/(b-1), norm and spectral radius sqrt(b), and spectrum {b^(1-k/2):k>=1} union {0}. Every nonzero spectral value is a simple eigenvalue; 0 is not an eigenvalue and lies in the continuous spectrum. Under the declared replication sum, block statistic, fixed Fisher norm, and log block scale, k=1 is relevant, k=2 marginal, and k>=3 irrelevant; the theorem is a linear tangent statement and does not extend to correlated, multivariate-anisotropic, or gauge-mixed blocks.

claims.falsifier: A Hermite mode violating the Mehler conditional-expectation identity, incompleteness of the claimed spectral closure, a nonzero vector in the kernel, a proof that 0 is an eigenvalue, or a correlated or multivariate instance presented as an instance of the scalar theorem.

Exponent invariance under a change of comparison trivialization requires tempered scalar mode normalization together with subexponential distortion of the complete trivialization and its inverse. No Oseledets splitting is asserted; the multiplicative ergodic theorem is invoked only conditionally with its full measurable and integrability hypotheses named.

claims.quantifiers: Every van-Fraassen-dependent interpretive sentence in the revised manuscript.
claims.falsifier: A checked primary-source passage deriving the idle-wheel rule from constructive empiricism or a surviving manuscript sentence attributing that entailment to van Fraassen.

claims.statement: The PDF keyword metadata removes or explicitly reconciles emergent time with the manuscript's refusal to identify information duration or RG depth with physical time.
claims.quantifiers: The released metadata and every scope disclaimer.
claims.falsifier: A metadata/source scan finding the unreconciled keyword.

claims.statement: Each multi-claim paragraph has one visibly scoped status per governed claim; the RG relevance trichotomy is DEFINITION, and the operational-trace route is OPEN with controlled settlement conditions.
claims.quantifiers: Every affected paragraph and status entry.
claims.falsifier: A status scan finding stacked tags with ambiguous scope, an ESTABLISHED tag on an interpretive position, or an uncontrolled operational-holonomy claim.

claims.statement: Status tags render as unbreakable units and no released page hyphenates a status token across lines.
claims.quantifiers: Every rendered status tag in the released PDF.
claims.falsifier: A visual or text-extraction audit finding a broken status token.

claims.statement: Generated auxiliary files are ignored or freshly produced in the release build and no stale tracked auxiliary is treated as current evidence.
claims.quantifiers: Every generated TeX auxiliary and release build.
claims.falsifier: A stale tracked auxiliary influencing or misdescribing the released build.

claims.statement: The base Fisher-defect residual delta_02 - delta_01 - f_01^* delta_12 equals Delta_12(v,v) - Delta_12(ubar,ubar) in three equivalent exact forms, where v is the pushed fine jet and ubar = v + A the coarse jet; the sign of the quadratic term is coupled to the choice of cross-term argument, and a convention-mixed expression exceeds the true residual by exactly 2 Delta_12(A,A). The sharp base cocycle holds if and only if Delta_12(v,v)=Delta_12(ubar,ubar), equivalently Delta_12(A,2v+A)=0. This is a quadratic-form equality unconditionally and an equal-seminorm criterion only under the Markov/positive-semidefinite hypothesis. Vanishing stage-one anomaly, a Fisher-lossless second arrow, and containment of the stage-one anomaly in the radical of Delta_12 are each sufficient and none is necessary. The underlying vertical cocycle is unconditional.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite composable sequence of scale arrows, both belief and model channels, and every related section triple.
claims.falsifier: A printed correction term differing from the two admissible conventions; a claimed necessity of a vanishing stage-one anomaly, refuted by the three-level instance whose residual -2a(a+1)/3 vanishes at a = -1 with anomaly -2; or a telescoping identity in h_j - f^*_{jk} h_k presented as a verification of the sharp base cocycle, which it is not, being unconditional.

claims.statement: The typed curve objects are pairwise distinct: a nonstationary curve inside one fixed statistical fiber is vertical, while the zero total velocity is stationary; a total-space curve over a nonconstant base curve is horizontal only relative to a chosen connection and is otherwise mixed; a base curve carries no verticality or horizontality predicate at all; and a curve of configurations lives in a section space, so verticality statements about it are statements about its adjoint evaluation at a fixed context. The pointwise vertical, horizontal, mixed, and stationary cases partition every parameter value, whereas the interval-level labels obtained by quantifying them are not exhaustive. Verticality is connection free; horizontality and the mixed decomposition are not. The contextual base remains fixed and timeless.
claims.quantifiers: Every connected parameter interval, every principal connection, and every curve of each of the four kinds.
claims.falsifier: An interval-level curve label applied where the pointwise type varies; a verticality or horizontality predicate applied to a base curve or to a configuration curve; or a claim that the interval-level labels are exhaustive.

claims.statement: Equality of objectives does not intertwine natural gradients, because the differential is metric free and the gradient is not. Under functional compatibility F_l = chi_l . F_{l+1} . R_l with chi_l' > 0 on an open set containing the orbit, and with R_l a surjective submersion with closed orbit-tangent splitting, horizontal conformality with dilation varphi_l > 0 is SUFFICIENT for semiconjugacy with factor a_l = chi_l' varphi_l^2 > 0, the Riemannian-submersion case being varphi_l = 1. Under pointwise Markov hypotheses, configuration-tier conformality is equivalent exactly to the integrated bilinear/Gram identity int sum_x w_x Delta_F(Z_x,W_x) dmu=(1-varphi_l^2)G_l(Z,W) on the declared horizontal tangent space. Pointwise conformality follows only with a declared compactly-supported-localizable tangent module and full-support measure (or a separately declared sign condition); a finite span can satisfy the integrated identity without its pointwise form. None is automatic.
claims.quantifiers: Every pair of C2 objectives and strong configuration metrics and every submersive coarse configuration map satisfying the displayed functional and metric hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: A gradient intertwining claimed from equality of objectives alone, refuted by the identity map on R^2 with one objective and metrics diag(1,1) and diag(1,kappa); a pointwise-conformality conclusion from the finite two-context Markov witness with pullback Fishers 1/4 and 3/4 but integrated ratio 1/2; a semiconjugacy claimed from a submersion without a metric compatibility hypothesis; or a claim that the sufficient conditions are also necessary.

claims.statement: Scale depth l, an orbit parameter r, and Fisher duration tau^(l) are distinct typed quantities: l is a discrete scale index, r is a chosen oriented parameter on a selected orbit, and tau is metric-relative arc length from a chosen origin. After metric, origin, orientation, and parameterized-path choices, tau may be a function of r. It is not canonically determined by an unparameterized orbit or by scale depth, and is neither a contextual-base function nor physical time. Strict monotonicity of tau does not make it a regular coordinate.
claims.quantifiers: Every regular oriented orbit segment with a selected configuration metric, path, origin, orientation, and finite configuration Fisher speeds, at every declared scale depth.
claims.falsifier: A claim that tau cannot be a function of r after the auxiliary choices; a canonical duration asserted for an unparameterized orbit or for scale depth alone; an inversion of tau at a Fisher-null point, refuted by h_s = 4x^2 dx^2 giving tau(r) = r^2 with nondifferentiable inverse; a global clock asserted without a closed clock one-form of vanishing periods; or any identification of tau with a physical clock reading.

claims.statement: Any comparison of INTEGRATED configuration metrics or durations across scales requires the two separately declared conditions (X1) f_# mu = mubar and (X2) wbar_x o f <= w_x for both channels. The weight term is typed as (w_x-(wbar_x o f)) f^*hbar_x. Neither condition follows from any fiberwise contraction theorem, and either failing reverses the comparison even at zero horizontal defect and zero information loss.
claims.quantifiers: Every scale arrow at which an integrated configuration metric or a duration comparison is asserted, and both channels.
claims.falsifier: An integrated cross-scale comparison asserted with f_# mu != mubar, refuted on the disjoint union of two copies of the line with point masses on different components; or with wbar_x o f > w_x in some channel, which breaks positivity of the typed two-channel difference. A witness typed on a zero-dimensional base is inadmissible, since the symmetric square of its cotangent bundle is zero.

claims.statement: For a separately declared smooth gauge-equivariant coarse configuration map realized as a fiberwise barycenter, the exact defect between the fine and coarse integrated metrics is nonnegative under chart joint convexity, and equals the sum of a channel-loss term, a weight-gap term, and a context Jensen-variance term, each separately nonnegative, when the coarse fiber metric is constant in the chart. Generic averaging is NOT a contraction without joint convexity or weight domination. At the declared finite-dimensional additive tier the map is linear, hence smooth, and is gauge equivariant exactly for the affine coefficient translations xi->xi+L_l g when E L_l=L_{l+1}; metric compatibility is E^T Phibar E <= Phi.
claims.quantifiers: Every declared coarse configuration map used in a metric or duration comparison, and every configuration tangent.
claims.falsifier: An averaging or variational coarse map asserted to lose information in a chart where the fiber Fisher integrand is not jointly convex, refuted by the Gaussian moment chart with coarse-to-fine ratio 20000/10201 at delta = 1/100 and supremum equal to the block size; a claimed affine-gauge equivariance without E L_l=L_{l+1}; an identification of the law-chart mixture defect with a chart-barycenter defect; or a Markov predicate attached to a barycenter that admits no realizing kernel.
